newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: POLL - Petron H1 seen up despite competition.
newsitem.headline: POLL - Petron H1 seen up despite competition.

text.p: Petron Corp, the Philippines' biggest oil refiner, will report a higher net for the first half of the year despite having its energies diverted by a fierce fight with rivals at petrol stations, analysts said on Friday.

A Reuters poll of seven stock brokerages, four of which gave first-half forecasts, showed Petron was expected to post a 14.65 percent rise in net profit for the first six months of 1997 to 2.27 billion pesos ($86 million) from 1.98 billion a year ago.
But of those surveyed, two -- Angping Securities and Guoco Securities -- said they had downgraded their full year forecast after lower-than-expected sales volume in the first quarter.
Petron posted only a slight rise in first-quarter sales this year to 1.05 billion pesos -- most of which came from non-operating income -- compared to last year's 1.03 billion pesos.
For the full year, Petron was seen posting a 9.21 percent gain in profit to 4.67 billion pesos from 4.24 billion in 1996.
ING Baring Securities analyst Giovanni dela Rosa said he expected slightly improved sales volume in the second quarter to offset the lower volumes in the first quarter.
Guoco Securities research head Saturnino Mejia attributed Petron's lower sales in the first three months to increasing competition, especially in the liquefied petroleum gas market.
"I think they are beginning to feel competition becoming more aggressive but it will take time to outpace Petron," Sapphire Securities analyst Henry Ong said.
In February, the Philippine government released the oil industry from decades of control and allowed firms to make new investments and fix their own product prices.
Since then Petron has been in a price war with its two rivals, Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corp and Caltex Philippines Inc. Deregulation has also meant that new players are crowding into the market.
Analysts said a blast at a Petron refinery near Manila in mid-June was unlikely to affect earnings. Petron said the incident was not disrupting supplies.
"They have enough inventory so the impact of the explosion at its catalyst cooler is negligible, except of course if repairs exceed their month-long target," said Mejia.

Despite the projected rise in profits for the first half, some analysts are now lukewarm on a stock which was the darling of small Filipino investors when the company launched its initial public offering five years ago.
Petron's IPO was such a hit that it enticed thousands of first-time investors to the equities market.

"It's stable but there's not much growth. So we are not bullish. We were recommending buy on Petron before and now we're a long-term buy," said Alexis Cabel, analyst at Angping & Associates Securities.
ING Barings said the one bright spot about Petron was that it was gaining market share in the retail market where it is considered the weakest.
"We expect double-digit growth in the reseller market for the year although total overall sales volume may be lower," said ING's Dela Rosa.
